messages:
alex_support: FYI escalation from a customer on Dedicated/private deploy — they see intermittent JSON parse errors when using JSON mode + streaming. Happens across Python and TS clients. Error is 'Unexpected token \u0000 in JSON at position X' when the stream ends. Repro steps from customer attached below.

alex_support: Repro (from customer):
```
# python client streaming read
for chunk in client.stream_generate(json_mode=True):
    buffer += chunk
# sometimes buffer contains embedded nulls and whole JSON parse fails
json.loads(buffer)
```

ryan_eng: thanks. which model/version and runtime? any request_id or example response blob we can inspect? is this high-latency or high-QPS path?

alex_support: customer says runtime v3.12.0 (private), KV prefix caching ON, burst traffic ~600rps, most failures on long-lived streaming responses (>4k tokens). sent sample bytes (hex) in support ticket.

sophie_sdk: I vaguely remember a similar root cause — when KV cache frames are concatenated on reuse we sometimes leave trailing zero bytes in the last buffer slice if the buffer pool is larger than payload, and those \u0000 bytes get written to the stream. JSON-mode streaming consumers that naively concat then parse will break.

june_ml: copied the sample and decoded hex, here's a trimmed excerpt showing the problem:
```
... 7b 22 63 6f 6e 74 65 6e 74 22 3a 20 22 66 6f 6f 22 7d 00 00 00 00
// -> {"content": "foo"}\u0000\u0000\u0000\u0000
```
That sequence will break strict JS JSON.parse and Python's json.loads.

sophie_sdk: can we get eng-runtime to either trim trailing null bytes on flush for JSON-mode streams or change the framing so consumer doesn't see pad bytes? For immediate mitigation we can change SDK streaming parse to treat trailing NULs as whitespace for json_mode. Safer to treat NULs between frames as ignorable in the parser.

ryan_eng: agree. I'll reproduce locally. quick note: this only affects json_mode + streaming + buffer reuse + certain sequence lengths. Not a decode bug in serde per-se but in the writer side leaving pad bytes.

ryan_eng: local repro (small Go test) I used to validate behavior:
```
// create a writer that writes payload then writes padding bytes from buffer pool
w.Write([]byte(`{"content":"bar"}`))
w.Write([]byte{0,0,0}) // pad from pool reuse
// client reads stream as ndjson/json-mode and fails
```
Using encoding/json.Decode in Go will error on the NULs.

sophie_sdk: Patch plan:
- eng-runtime: trim trailing 0x00 bytes on each JSON-mode flush (fast guard).
- SDKs (py/ts/go): make streaming JSON mode tolerant by trimming trailing NULs before final parse and skipping zero-only fragments. Add a feature flag `json_mode_tolerant_nulls` default true for now.

ryan_eng: opened runtime PR fix/null-trim-serializer. Will run canary build in canary pool.

deploy-bot: deploys/runtime fix/null-trim-serializer -> canary started (post=1918765499) :rocket:

sophie_sdk: I'll cut quick Py+TS patch to tolerate nulls on parse and add unit tests with embedded 0x00 bytes. Will tag SDKs to test against canary.

alex_support: escalation owner here. I've told customer we'll try canary at ~15:00 PT and will call them. Marked S2 because on Dedicated and affecting production traffic.

ryan_eng: after canary validation if all good we'll backport to v3.11.x and push SDK patches then notify support to push to customer.

alex_support: thanks team — I'll update ticket with canary link and ask for quick feedback. :thumbsup:
